awd_titl_txt: SBIR Phase I: Multiplexed High Throughput Discovery of Functional RNA-Targeting Small Molecules Via Next-Generation Sequencing
awd_abstract_narration:
The broader impact/commercial potential of this Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Phase I project is to address currently untreatable diseases by developing small molecule drugs that modulate RNA. Despite advances in genomic medicine, many disease-causing proteins remain undruggable using conventional approaches. By targeting RNA instead of proteins, this project could enable therapeutic interventions for diseases lacking treatment options, including certain cancers and neurological disorders. The technology platform will provide a scalable method to identify RNA-targeting small molecules, accelerating drug discovery and potentially creating a new class of oral medications. The commercial impact extends beyond therapeutic applications, as the screening platform could become an industry-standard tool for RNA drug discovery, stimulating broader pharmaceutical innovation.

This Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Phase I project aims to develop a next-generation sequencing platform for discovering small molecules that target RNA. The project addresses two challenges: demonstrating that small molecules binding to messenger RNA can modulate protein expression in cells, and developing a high-throughput screening method to identify such molecules and their optimal RNA targets. The research will establish an assay that can detect RNA-drug interactions and identify which RNA structures are most amenable to binding. The technical approach integrates RNA biochemistry with next-generation sequencing to create a multiplexed screening platform. If successful, this project will establish a novel approach to RNA-targeted drug discovery, providing starting points for developing therapies against disease targets previously considered undruggable.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Many of today's most challenging diseases are driven by proteins that cannot be targeted by existing medicines. While RNA-based therapies such as antisense oligonucleotides and siRNAs can modulate these proteins, they require injection, reach only a limited number of tissues, and are costly, leaving millions of patients without effective treatment options. Endura Therapeutics is developing a new class of covalent small molecule drugs that bind RNA to reduce the production of disease-causing proteins. Because small molecules can be taken orally and distributed broadly throughout the body, this approach has the potential to reach tissues inaccessible to current RNA therapies while dramatically improving affordability and convenience for patients.
Through this NSF SBIR Phase I award, Endura accomplished two key objectives that validate this novel therapeutic approach. First, we demonstrated that covalent modification of messenger RNA by a small molecule can meaningfully reduce protein production in human cells, confirming the core mechanism that underpins our drug modality. Second, we established a high-throughput screening assay based on next-generation sequencing that can detect covalent small molecule interactions with RNA in living cells. This assay enables rapid, multiplexed discovery of drug candidates across numerous RNA targets simultaneously, a capability that did not previously exist for this class of molecules.
These results validate covalent small molecules as a viable new modality for targeting RNA and open the door to drug discovery programs against proteins that have long been considered undruggable, including those implicated in certain cancers and neurological disorders. The screening platform developed through this work provides a scalable foundation for identifying and optimizing drug candidates, with the potential to catalyze a new wave of oral, affordable therapies. Endura Therapeutics is now advancing this platform toward internal drug programs and partnerships with the goal of bringing novel treatments to patients with high unmet medical need.
